newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila in talks with Seoul, Beijing on defector.
newsitem.headline: Manila in talks with Seoul, Beijing on defector.

text.p: The Philippines has told China and South Korea it will provide sanctuary to North Korean defector Hwang Jang-yop for "as short as possible" and is awaiting their response, President Fidel Ramos said on Wednesday.
Hwang has been in a secret hideaway since China spirited him into the Philippines on Tuesday last week after he defected to the South Korean consulate in Beijing on February 12.

"We will provide all the security and hospitality that we accord to foreign visitors and at the same, however, we have asked that the authorities concerned in the two countries consider that his stay here be as short as possible," Ramos said at his weekly news conference.

Armed forces intelligence chief Major-General Benjamin Libarnes, the Filipino officer in charge of Hwang's security, said the 73-year-old North Korean was under heavy guard in his hideout but refused to say where he was.
Fears he could be a target of Pyongyang hitmen have spurred tight security around him.
South Korean officials said last week Hwang would stay in the Philippines at least until the start of April.
